newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish May c/a hit by dividend payouts.
newsitem.headline: Swedish May c/a hit by dividend payouts.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, said on Monday that dividend pay-outs from foreigners' stakes in Swedish companies pushed Sweden's current account into a 1.5-billion-crown deficit in May.

Dividend pay-outs prompted a negative outflow of 6.3 billion crowns in May 1997, compared with 5.2 billion in May 1996, the central bank said after the surprise current account deficit. Analysts had forecast a 1.1 billion crown surplus.
The bank said the current account surplus for the first five months of this year totalled 20 billion crowns, 1.5 billion crowns lower than in the comparative 1996 period.

"The lower surplus can be explained mainly by weaker Services revenue as well as increased transfers overseas. The trade balance, on the other hand, shows a surplus for the first five months of the year that is around 1.1 billion crowns higher than expected," the bank said.
